passage_title: Holding Force of Moulded Clips after Repeated Opening
passage:
A clip moulded from a stiff plastic grips a card between two jaws. The holding force of a clip is the force, in newtons (N), needed to pull a standard card straight out of the closed clip. Repeatedly opening and closing a clip changes its holding force. Clips of four designs, labeled Design P through Design S, were tested. Every clip was moulded from the same plastic, in the same mould, and from the same batch of material; the four designs differ only in the shape of the hinge that joins the two jaws.

Experiment 1. A clip of each design was opened and closed 0, 200, 400, 600, or 800 times. The holding force of the clip was then measured at 20 °C. Three clips were tested at each combination of design and number of cycles; the three values agreed to within 0.1 N, and their mean is plotted. The results are shown in Figure 1.

Experiment 2. Clips of each design were opened and closed 400 times as in Experiment 1. Half of those clips were then held at 10 °C and the other half at 40 °C for 1 hr, and the holding force of each clip was measured at the temperature at which it had been held. The results are shown in Figure 2.

passage_title: Holding Force of Moulded Clips after Repeated Opening
passage:
A clip moulded from a stiff plastic grips a card between two jaws. The holding force of a clip is the force, in newtons (N), needed to pull a standard card straight out of the closed clip. Repeatedly opening and closing a clip changes its holding force. Clips of four designs, labeled Design P through Design S, were tested. Every clip was moulded from the same plastic, in the same mould, and from the same batch of material; the four designs differ only in the shape of the hinge that joins the two jaws.

Experiment 1. A clip of each design was opened and closed 0, 200, 400, 600, or 800 times. The holding force of the clip was then measured at 20 °C. Three clips were tested at each combination of design and number of cycles; the three values agreed to within 0.1 N, and their mean is plotted. The results are shown in Figure 1.

Experiment 2. Clips of each design were opened and closed 400 times as in Experiment 1. Half of those clips were then held at 10 °C and the other half at 40 °C for 1 hr, and the holding force of each clip was measured at the temperature at which it had been held. The results are shown in Figure 2.

passage_title: Holding Force of Moulded Clips after Repeated Opening
passage:
A clip moulded from a stiff plastic grips a card between two jaws. The holding force of a clip is the force, in newtons (N), needed to pull a standard card straight out of the closed clip. Repeatedly opening and closing a clip changes its holding force. Clips of four designs, labeled Design P through Design S, were tested. Every clip was moulded from the same plastic, in the same mould, and from the same batch of material; the four designs differ only in the shape of the hinge that joins the two jaws.

Experiment 1. A clip of each design was opened and closed 0, 200, 400, 600, or 800 times. The holding force of the clip was then measured at 20 °C. Three clips were tested at each combination of design and number of cycles; the three values agreed to within 0.1 N, and their mean is plotted. The results are shown in Figure 1.

Experiment 2. Clips of each design were opened and closed 400 times as in Experiment 1. Half of those clips were then held at 10 °C and the other half at 40 °C for 1 hr, and the holding force of each clip was measured at the temperature at which it had been held. The results are shown in Figure 2.
